text: When taking pictures, aperture and shutter speed are important elements of the exposure triangle. Aperture is the size of the hole in the lens that lets light into the camera. The larger the aperture, the more light that can enter the camera and the shallower the depth of field. Shutter speed is the amount of time the camera's shutter is open. A fast shutter speed can freeze motion, while a slow shutter speed can create motion blur. Knowing the relationship between aperture and shutter speed is essential for creating visually compelling images.
